extracted.intended_audience: writers, critics, and educated readers seeking guidance on creating or recognising comedy and the comic spirit
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the comic spirit: how to perceive, write, and evaluate Comedy (distinct from satire, irony, and humour), with notes on tone, scope, targets, and national/style differences. Useful for playwrights, prose writers, and critics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for Comic perception
rubrics_metrics.description: You may estimate your capacity for Comic perception by being able to detect the ridicule of them you love, without loving them less: and more by being able to see yourself somewhat ridiculous in dear eyes, and accepting the correction their image of you proposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comic-sensed person can perceive ridicule within affection and accept self-ridicule; this capacity distinguishes comic perception from harsher modes that alienate warmth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sliding into Satire
rubrics_metrics.description: If you detect the ridicule, and your kindliness is chilled by it, you are slipping into the grasp of Satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire is a moral, often bile-filled attack; keep kindliness present if you want Comedy rather than a satiric blow. Satire attacks to wound rather than to perceive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise and use Irony carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: If instead of falling foul of the ridiculous person with a satiric rod, to make him writhe and shriek aloud, you prefer to sting him under a semi-caress, by which he shall in his anguish be rendered dubious whether indeed anything has hurt him, you are an engine of Irony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irony uses a semi-caressing sting and ambiguity; it differs from Comedy (which is perceptive) and Satire (which is openly condemnatory). Beware of 'foppish' or leering irony that reveals intent and thus fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Humour from Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you laugh all round him, tumble him, roll him about, deal him a smack, and drop a tear on him, own his likeness to you and yours to your neighbour, spare him as little as you shun, pity him as much as you expose, it is a spirit of Humour that is moving you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humour embraces pity and tenderness alongside exposure; it comforts and tucks up the feelings, often fusing tragic feeling with laughable situations. Comedy, by contrast, addresses the intellect more narrowly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic as governing perceptive spirit (not identical to satire/irony/humour)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic, which is the perceptive, is the governing spirit, awakening and giving aim to these powers of laughter, but it is not to be confounded with them: it enfolds a thinner form of them, differing from satire, in not sharply driving into the quivering sensibilities, and from humour, in not comforting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the Comic as an intellectual, perceptive stance: it quickens the mind without the moral savagery of satire or the consolatory warmth of humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy addresses the intellect through social contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic poet addresses the still narrower enclosure of men's intellects, with reference to the operation of the social world upon their characters... they refresh the intellect they quicken to detect their comedy, by force of the contrast they offer between themselves and the wiser world about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy should present clear contrasts between character and social wisdom so the intellect recognises the comic idea; examples given include Alceste, Tartuffe, and Fielding's method of correcting sentimental writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: focus on the present social scene, not on beginnings or endings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic poet is in the narrow field, or enclosed square, of the society he depicts; and he is not concerned with beginnings or endings or surroundings, but with what you are now weaving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the comic work to an intelligible, bounded social situation. Comedy gains force from focused present-action depiction rather than sprawling context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone of Comic laughter: impersonal, polite, often a smile
rubrics_metrics.description: The laughter of satire is a blow in the back or the face. The laughter of Comedy is impersonal and of unrivalled politeness, nearer a smile; often no more than a smile. It laughs through the mind, for the mind directs it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for an urbane, intellectually-directed laugh rather than coarse derision; the desired effect is a 'silvery' or 'tempered' laughter rather than a raw roar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid derisive laughter at misfortune
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidents of a kind casting ridicule on our unfortunate nature instead of our conventional life, provoke derisive laughter, which thwarts the Comic idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make victims' misfortunes merely objects of derision. The Comic should target social pretension or incongruity, not cruelty toward suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of true Comedy: awakens thoughtful laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: One excellent test of the civilization of a country, as I have said, I take to be the flourishing of the Comic idea and Comedy; and the test of true Comedy is that it shall awaken thoughtful laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate comedy by whether it produces reflective, mind-directed laughter rather than only coarse amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator's attitude: sober liking and sober estimate of humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: To understand his work and value it, you must have a sober liking of your kind and a sober estimate of our civilized qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comic poet/creator should exhibit affectionate restraint and measured judgment toward human foibles; contempt or excess hostility undermines Comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint, measure and taste (mesure et goût)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy, or in any form the Comic spirit, will then come to them to cut some figures out of the block... The French lay marked stress on mesure et gout, and they own how much they owe to Moliere for leading them in simple justness and taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate measure and taste; avoid grossness and overstatement that turn comedy into farce or brutality.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Comic spirit should 'eye but not touch' (avoid acting out into farce)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic spirit eyes but does not touch it. Put into action, it would be farcical. It is too gross for Comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy often points out absurdities without physically or vindictively enacting them; keep a mental/interpretive distance rather than gratuitous staging of degradation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the stage as corrective discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a benefit to men in taking the lessons of Comedy in congregations, for it enlivens the wits; and to writers it is beneficial, for they must have a clear scheme... And writing for the stage would be a corrective of a too-incrusted scholarly style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing for performance forces clear structure, economy of language, and attention to public effect—use stage-discipline to sharpen comic writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclose the comic idea for portability and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not know that the fly in amber is of any particular use, but the Comic idea enclosed in a comedy makes it more generally perceptible and portable, and that is an advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the comic idea so it can be apprehended in a single, coherent artistic unit (e.g., a play or a clearly-finished scene), which helps audiences grasp its lesson and delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware crude realism that confusedly presents moral ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern French comedy is commendable for the directness of the study of actual life... A consequence of this crude, though well-meant, realism is the collision of the writers in their scenes and incidents... The triumph of a candid realism is to show him no hero. If, however, you think at all, after the curtain has fallen, you are likely to think that the Aventurieres have a case to plead against him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adopting realistic study of life, ensure the comic framing makes the intended judgment or interpretation clear; otherwise realism can produce unintended sympathy for the wrong character and undermine the comic point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate breadth of comic appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: We know the degree of refinement in men by the matter they will laugh at, and the ring of the laugh; but we know likewise that the larger natures are distinguished by the great breadth of their power of laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mature comic sensibility values a wide range of comic models (from Aristophanes to Moliere to Shakespeare); both producing and appreciating comedy benefits from broad exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate national/style resources (taste vs. force)
rubrics_metrics.description: The national disposition is for hard-hitting... But the Comic is a different spirit... The French controversialist is a polished swordsman... The German irony is a missile of terrific tonnage... The French lay stress on mesure et gout...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of stylistic/national tendencies (English satire, French measure, German force) and adopt those elements that serve the comic aim—measure, directness, or robust contrast—without importing the attendant faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid capriciousness when humour touches history or society
rubrics_metrics.description: The humourist of high has an embrace of contrasts beyond the scope of the Comic poet... This vast power of his, built up of the feelings and the intellect in union, is often wanting in proportion and in discretion. Humourists touching upon History or Society are given to be capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When employing humour that ranges into history or society, guard proportion and discretion; unchecked sentiment or caprice can undermine the intellectual comic effect.
